subject: Sandboxed capture, ephemeral keys, and derivative assurance
messages:
From: Clara Diaz <clara.diaz@healix.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@healix.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: operational proof for non-training and ephemeral capture

Hi Aisha / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Healix is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move a pilot forward we need two concrete assurances in writing that our security team will validate:

1) A no-training / model-improvement commitment for the pilot workload (including any debug/logging telemetry) and a short description of how you enforce it operationally (e.g., flags, tenant isolation, routing).

2) An operational evidence pack showing that captured inputs (prompts) and model outputs are only retained ephemerally for debugging, that KV/prefix caches are disabled for our tenant, and what retention windows/log export paths exist (S3, onshore only, encryption-at-rest).

Can you share a short proofflow (diagram + checklist) and the named artifacts you supply to customers for audits? We will need this to complete our internal DPA addendum review. Attached a sample data-flow from our side for context.

Also flag any exceptions (debug exports to engineering Slack, on-call dumps, analytics telemetry) and whether they can be disabled.

Best,
Clara
Director of Product & Security
Healix.ai

Attachment: data_flow_diagram.png (image)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>

Folks — forwarding Healix's ask. Short summary: they want an operator-level proof that (a) we will not use their pilot data to train or improve models, and (b) that capture is sandboxed/ephemeral with KV cache disabled for the tenant.

Ben: Healix is a key pilot for the healthcare vertical — please keep them informed on timing.

David/Kim: can you assemble a single-page proofflow + the usual artifacts we hand to SOC/pilot customers (ops playbook + retention table + export controls)? Specific asks from the mail: disable on-call debug dumps and verify onshore-only S3 export if we must provide any exports.

Happy to jump on a quick sync if needed.

—Aisha
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

-----Original message attached above-----

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Clara Diaz <clara.diaz@healix.ai>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@healix.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 15:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: operational proof for non-training and ephemeral capture

Clara / team — thanks for the clear list. Summary of what Redwood can provide for the pilot (operational details below). I'll attach the proofflow and ops playbook to this thread.

Quick answers up front:
- No-training commitment: Redwood will add a pilot-specific DPA addendum clause that prevents any of Healix's data from being used for model training or tuning. The clause will be tenant-scoped and enforced by a serving-policy flag in the control plane (we will provide the addendum draft).
- Operational enforcement: the serving runtime sets a tenant-level "learning=false" flag. When set: KV/prefix caching is disabled, gradients/metrics used for model updates are discarded, and telemetry exports that could be used for training are dropped at the ingestion point.
- Retention and exports: default ephemeral retention for chat/prompt data is 7 days for pilot tenants; for Healix we can set to 24 hours. Any debug exports (engineer dumps, trace zips) are opt-in and require two-person approval; by default those are disabled for the pilot. All exports for Healix will be routed to an onshore-only S3 bucket under Healix's account, encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys (CMK).

Artifacts attached: sandbox_proofflow_v1.pdf (diagram + checklist), ops_playbook.xlsx (retention table + roles + emergency export SOP). Highlights from the proofflow:
- Serving policy enforcement (control plane flag)
- Runtime sandbox (request tagging + prefix routing)
- KV cache disabled per-tenant; ephemeral KV used only for ephemeral session state and auto-cleared after 30s of inactivity
- Sampling/telemetry gate at ingestion that blocks any request-level data from pipeline used for model improvement

Next steps:
1) Please review attached proofflow for any gaps we missed.
2) We will draft a short DPA addendum and route for legal review (Kimberly already on copy).
3) If Healix needs us to sign a specific contractual no-training clause, we can include the precise text in the addendum and provide audit screenshots of the tenant flag and S3 export routing.

—David
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sandbox_proofflow_v1.pdf, ops_playbook.xlsx

Thanks David — this is super helpful and addresses our main concerns. A few quick items:

- Confirmed we want the 24-hour retention window.
- Please include the exact DPA addendum language referencing tenant-level "learning=false" enforcement. Our legal team will need the wording to close the procurement review.
- We may ask for an export audit screenshot (S3 bucket + CMK ID) during the signing step; that's fine on our side.

Can we book a 30-min call next week to walk through the proofflow with our security engineer? Available Mon/Tue mornings PST. Also, will you send the DocuSign link for the DPA addendum when ready?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Clara
Director of Product & Security, Healix.ai
